newsitem.title: INDIA: India Arvind to merge associate firm.
newsitem.headline: India Arvind to merge associate firm.

text.p: Indian textile major Arvind Mills Ltd on Monday said it planned to merge with itself its associate Arvind Intex Ltd.
"Arvind Intex Ltd, a 49 percent associate of Arvind Mills, is proposed to be merged to achieve synergies of operations," it said in a statement.
It said Arvind Intex met 40 percent of the yarn requirements of Arvind Mills' denim business.
Textile analysts said the merger will have little impact on the company's operations as the equity addition is minimal.
"The improved performance of the company should be viewed in the backdrop of a general decline in corporate performance," it quoted Arvind managing director Sanjay Lalbhai as saying.

"Gross margins improved under the influence of several strategic and operating initiatives taken by the company such as thrust on building brands, upgrading product mix and control on operating costs," Lalbhai was quoted as saying.
A fall in cotton prices also helped the firm, Arvind said.
"Arvind is today the largest company in the readymade garment segment and this position will further be consolidated in the current year," the company statement said.
"With the expansion of denim capacity by 40 million meters, Arvind is now amongst the top three denim producers in the world with a production capacity of 120 million meters per annum."

Arvind is building two co-generation power plants to achieve self-sufficiency in power. The company recently completed a floating rate note issue of $125 million and with this has tied up all the required funds, it said.
After a board meeting on Monday, Arvind said its net profit rose to 1.27 billion rupees for the year ended March 31, 1997, up from 1.13 billion rupees a year ago.
It maintained the dividend at 4.50 rupees per share.
The turnover rose to 8.63 billion rupees from 7.09 billion rupees in the previous year.
"Operating profit was 1.86 billion rupees, a rise of 81 percent," Arvind said. The earnings per share improved to 12.70 rupees from 11.40 rupees a year ago, the company said.
